Definition: The completeness of a specific attribute, defined as the ratio of present values for that attribute to the total number of records.
The completeness of a specific record, measured as the ratio of present values for required attributes in that record to the total number of required attributes (K).
The overall completeness of the dataset — the average attribute completeness or total proportion of non-missing values across all N records and M_req required attributes.
Measures reliability of a single source over N observations as the Mean Absolute Error between observed values and expected/reference values.
Measures how much the data fluctuates relative to its average value over a defined time window, using the coefficient of variation. Lower CV indicates higher temporal stability.
The proportion of the dataset that consists of duplicate records, based on a defined set of key attributes.
The absolute number of duplicate records in a dataset.
Focuses on the storage of derivable data (e.g., storing both Date of Birth and Age is redundant since one can be derived from the other). Identified via schema analysis and data lineage.
Formula: N/A — identified through schema analysis and data lineage rather than a single universal formula

Definition: The proportion of values that are incorrect (do not match true reference values).
The proportion of values that are correct (match true reference values).
The average magnitude of the errors between data values and their corresponding true values (for numerical data).
The average of the squared errors; more sensitive to large errors than MAE.
The square root of the MSE, expressed in the same units as the original data.
The absolute time delay for a single data point/record between the real-world event and its availability in the target system.
The mean latency across N records over a specific period.
The proportion of data records that meet the specified latency SLA (i.e., records where L ≤ SLA_threshold).
For datasets requiring periodic updates, measures time elapsed since the last update relative to the expected update frequency. F ≤ 1 indicates fresh data.
The overall rate of consistency violations across all checks performed.
Formula: CVR = (Number of consistency violations detected / Total number of checks performed) × 100%

Definition: The overall consistency of the dataset, complementary to CVR.
Proportion of values adhering to the defined format.
Formula: FCR = (Number of values adhering to defined format / Total number of values checked) × 100%

Definition: Proportion of records satisfying defined logical rules.
Formula: LCR = (Number of records satisfying logical rules / Total records checked) × 100%

Definition: Proportion of calculations that are correct.
Formula: CCR = (Number of correct calculations / Total calculations checked) × 100%

Definition: Proportion of valid foreign key relationships across datasets.
Formula: RICR = (Number of valid foreign key relationships / Total foreign key relationships) × 100%

Definition: Proportion of records compliant with defined business rules.
Formula: BRCR = (Number of business rule compliant records / Total records checked) × 100%

Definition: Proportion of matching values across different systems.
Formula: DSR = (Number of matching values across systems / Total values compared) × 100%

Definition: Proportion of aligned master data records across systems.
Formula: MDAR = (Number of aligned master data records / Total master data records) × 100%

Definition: A composite metric based on completeness, accuracy, and consistency dimensions. Scores range from 0% (poor integrity) to 100% (perfect integrity). Equal weighting is assumed but weights can be adjusted per domain.
Sub-metric feeding into the Integrity Score composite.
Formula: Number of non-missing values / Total expected values

Definition: Sub-metric feeding into the Integrity Score composite. Counts values within expected ranges or formats.
Formula: Number of valid values / Total values

Definition: Sub-metric feeding into the Integrity Score composite. Counts records adhering to business rules (e.g., no duplicates, referential integrity).
Formula: Number of records adhering to business rules / Total records
